title: Gromov's h-principle for open ample relations via the key invariant P₀ P₁ P₂
intent: Reduce Gromov's h-principle for open ample first-order differential relations to a generic induction over the manifold by choosing three germ predicates P₀ P₁ P₂ (the invariant) that a local improvement step preserves and whose conjunction is exactly the conclusion, so the whole proof becomes 'define the invariant, prove it survives one step, hand it to the induction engine'.

children.name: _root_.exists_stability_dist
children.statement:
theorem _root_.exists_stability_dist {f : M → M'} (hf : Continuous f) :
    ∃ ε : M → ℝ, (∀ m, 0 < ε m) ∧ Continuous ε ∧
      ∀ x : M,
        ∃ φ : OpenSmoothEmbedding 𝓘(ℝ, E) E I M,
        ∃ ψ : OpenSmoothEmbedding 𝓘(ℝ, E') E' I' M',
          x ∈ range φ ∧
          ∀ (g : M → M'), (∀ m, dist (g m) (f m) < ε m) → range (g ∘ φ) ⊆ range ψ
children.note: `_root_.` is a namespace qualifier: the theorem is `exists_stability_dist` in the root namespace, written fully qualified because of the `open LocalisationData in` on the preceding line. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: every continuous map admits a positive continuous stability distance

children.name: OpenSmoothEmbedding.improve_formalSol
children.statement:
theorem OpenSmoothEmbedding.improve_formalSol (φ : OpenSmoothEmbedding 𝓘(ℝ, EM) EM IM M)
    (ψ : OpenSmoothEmbedding 𝓘(ℝ, EX) EX IX X) {R : RelMfld IM M IX X} (hRample : R.Ample)
    (hRopen : IsOpen R) {C : Set M} (hC : IsClosed C) {δ : M → ℝ} (hδ_pos : ∀ x, 0 < δ x)
    (hδ_cont : Continuous δ) {F : FormalSol R} (hFφψ : F.bs '' range φ ⊆ range ψ)
    (hFC : ∀ᶠ x near C, F.IsHolonomicAt x) {K₀ K₁ : Set EM} (hK₀ : IsCompact K₀)
    (hK₁ : IsCompact K₁) (hK₀K₁ : K₀ ⊆ interior K₁) :
    ∃ F' : HtpyFormalSol R,
      (∀ᶠ t near Iic (0 : ℝ), F' t = F) ∧
        (∀ᶠ t near Ici (1 : ℝ), F' t = F' 1) ∧
          (∀ᶠ x near C, ∀ t, F' t x = F x) ∧
            (∀ t, ∀ x ∉ φ '' K₁, F' t x = F x) ∧
              (∀ t x, dist ((F' t).bs x) (F.bs x) < δ x) ∧
                ∀ᶠ x near C ∪ φ '' K₀, (F' 1).IsHolonomicAt x

children.name: inductive_htpy_construction
children.statement:
theorem inductive_htpy_construction {X Y : Type*}
    [EMetricSpace X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X]
    (P₀ P₁ : ∀ x : X, Germ (𝓝 x) Y → Prop)
    (P₂ : ∀ p : ℝ × X, Germ (𝓝 p) Y → Prop)
    (hP₂ : ∀ (a b) (p : ℝ × X) (f : ℝ × X → Y), P₂ (a * p.1 + b, p.2) f →
      P₂ p fun p : ℝ × X ↦ f (a * p.1 + b, p.2))
    (hP₂' : ∀ t x (f : X → Y), P₀ x f → P₂ (t, x) fun p : ℝ × X ↦ f p.2)
    {f₀ : X → Y} (init : ∀ x, P₀ x f₀)
    (ind : ∀ x, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 x, ∀ K₁ ⊆ V, ∀ K₀ ⊆ interior K₁, IsCompact K₀ → IsCompact K₁ →
      ∀ (C : Set X) (f : X → Y), IsClosed C → (∀ x, P₀ x f) →
      (∀ᶠ x near C, P₁ x f) → ∃ F : ℝ → X → Y, (∀ t, ∀ x, P₀ x <| F t)
        ∧ (∀ᶠ x near C ∪ K₀, P₁ x <| F 1) ∧
      (∀ p, P₂ p ↿F) ∧ (∀ t, ∀ x ∉ K₁, F t x = f x) ∧
      (∀ᶠ t near Iic 0, F t = f) ∧ ∀ᶠ t near Ici 1, F t = F 1) :
    ∃ F : ℝ → X → Y, F 0 = f₀ ∧ (∀ t x, P₀ x (F t)) ∧ (∀ x, P₁ x (F 1)) ∧ ∀ p, P₂ p ↿F

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem of the form 'for every formal solution there is a homotopy to a holonomic one' (an h-principle / local-to-global statement), proved by a generic induction engine parameterized by predicates over germs.
applicability.use_when: the theorem is proved by an induction whose step does one local improvement, and the real content is a predicate (the invariant) that (a) implies the conclusion at the end, (b) is satisfied initially, and (c) is preserved by one step; the invariant is a conjunction of the target property with the side conditions (smoothness, agreement on a closed set, closeness) that make the step re-appliable.
applicability.avoid_when: there is no generic engine to hand the predicates to (then the induction itself is the work); the invariant is just the conclusion with no extra side conditions (the move collapses to plain induction); or the step changes the invariant in a way that needs per-index bookkeeping, which the engine's fixed three-predicate signature does not express.

claims.claim: The authors state the weak/strong split as a design choice: 'The weak version has ∀ x ∈ C, ∀ t : ℝ, 𝓕 t x = 𝓕₀ x while the strong one has ∀ᶠ x near C, ∀ t, 𝓕 t x = 𝓕₀ x. The strong version is easy to derive from the weak one if we prove the weak one for *all* closed sets, see RelMfld.satisfiesHPrinciple_of_weak below.'

consequences: The move replaces 'prove the h-principle' with three obligations: prove the invariant holds initially (init, Gromov.lean L79-84), prove it is preserved by one local step (the ind block, L87-165), and prove the two compatibility facts the engine needs (hP₂ affine-reindex, L67-78, and hP₂' slice, L85-86). The predicates must match the engine's exact signature (three predicates P₀ P₁ P₂ with the P₂ reindex and slice conditions). Failure mode: an invariant too weak to survive the step makes ind unprovable; too strong makes init or the boundary agreement fail. The empty-manifold corner still needs its own witness (emptyHtpyFormalSol).
